builds.name: Raven Adept
builds.desc:
With Rauðrraven+ and Triangle Adept, every vanilla green and grey except for Lucius, Niles, and Wrys dies when initiating the attack on him. Nino and Cecilia using Gronnblade+ cannot ORKO him, with Atk+ Cecilia doing 22 damage x2 with max buffs. Also, thanks to his innate tankiness, no vanilla non-blues with the exception of Sanaki and Lilina can kill this Henry in one round.
Due to his low Atk, he has trouble killing other units which is where Quick Riposte (QR) comes in to assist in those matchups. Taking either his default Ignis or Bonfire will also allow him to utilize his highly respectable Def to beef up his damage as well. Which skill you choose is dependent on a player's preference for timing. With no charges and an enemy who doubles him, one round of Quick Riposte will charge up Ignis for his next hit while Bonfire will activate on the the last hit of Quick Riposte. Henry appreciates the additional 30% from Ignis due to his abysmal Atk; however, Bonfire might help net him a few more kills with only the usage of QR. Since this is reliant on Henry needing to be doubled by the enemy, taking a Spd bane is Henry's preferred bane of choice so that he can activate more Bonfire-Quick Ripostes or having Ignis ready for his next attack.
Threaten Resistance will also help him gain kills on the enemy, and since he will most likely be at the front of your team tanking enemy damage, has a high likelihood of applying the buff. Even with Threaten Res, his low Atk still causes him to struggle to land OHKOs. Threaten Attack may be an alternative option then to boost his ability to tank better while other C-slots may also be considered depending on the needs of the team.
Reciprocal Aid can be used to siphon HP from teammates and maintain Quick Riposte if needed, or because of his high HP pool, as a large HP supply to other teammates who may need the HP. Other positioning assists such as Draw Back or Reposition may also be considered if a player prefers positioning assists.

builds.name: Offensively Viable Henry
builds.desc:
This is a way to make Henry actually viable for dishing out damage. I always thought Henry had nominal potential in the game, which is a shame because he was so great in Awakening.
This set revolves around the use of Rauðrblade+, to bump up his abysmal Atk to more devastating levels. This set works especially well if you have a mixed team using Tactics buffs, but regular buffing skills can work all right, too.
Reposition and Draw Back are mainly for getting your allies into the right position or saving them from danger. Since Henry has decent Def, he can tank a few physical hits. Not much else to it.
Moonbow and Glimmer are “bread ‘n’ butter” for the Blade tomes, and it’s no different for this set. Be mindful that Glimmer is dependent on damage dealt, so make sure Henry has all his buffs.
Death Blow 4 is a huge game-changer, sporting a hefty Atk+8 when initiating combat. For Henry, this is a blessing because it helps him compete with other Blade tome users. However, if you’re not willing to sacrifice a “well-earned” Brave Celica, then Death Blow 3 is still a reliable option.
Since Henry isn’t going to be doubleattacking anytime soon, he needs some Breaker skills to help him in that regard. Swordbreaker is the best thing for him because it helps him take care of those pesky, speedy sword units out there. Red Tomebreaker allows him to stand up to other red mages that may stand in his way, but because they’re rather uncommon, he should let a blue ally take care of them for him.
The C skill is completely flexible. Perhaps a Tactic skill can be administered to increase the efficacy of a Tactic team, but it’s completely yours to decide.
The Sacred Seal needs to be Atk+3, so he can push his Atk even further. He needs every buff he can get!
This isn’t a perfect set for Henry, and for several reasons. First, it takes a lot of investment. Taking Rauðrblade+ from Tharja is probably a weird decision to make because Tharja is already a superior character to Henry simply because she has better Atk and Spd. Also, if you plan to give him a Tactic skill, you have to make more sacrifices of 5☆ heroes (excluding Atk Tactic) to get them.
However, if you manage to put in the effort, Henry can actually deal some decent damage. With all the aforementioned buffs and such, his base damage can reach as high as 74.
Keep in mind that this set can be applied to any old mage; this is only a way to make Henry more offensive.

builds.name: Henry
builds.desc:
So lets begin, Henry may not have the highest of Attack in the game but with a plus atk nature and some investment he can actually be a good tank and deal some damage to enemies.
His weapon refine makes it easier for him to deal damage while adding a Guard affect to stop the enemies specials charging, keeping him alive and able to do more damage to the enemy, so keeping his personal weapon works best with this build.
For Henry's passive skills, skills like reposition works well to keep his allies from taking any damage after attacking and Harsh Command+ helps
to get rid of affects like Guard or effects like from the Flash+ Staff.
For Henry's Special skill Aether is a good choice for Arena scoring but it even though it has a high cool down with Henry's Tomes' Guard affect it means after a round or two of combat his special will be ready and he'll heal any damage taken from the foe.
For his A skill Life and death 3/4 increases his atk and spd so that he can keep up with some of the more medium-fast units in the game and because of his his defensive stats his Def/Res are still good enough for him to take a hit and counter-attack without being Killed.
For his B skill Quick Riposte 3 helps him be able to counter-attack twice, and because of his speed (if high enough) the foe only gets to attack once meaning anyone who attacks him will take more damage and lose their special charge as well.
For his C skill either Odd Atk wave or Odd spd wave 3 work best for this build as odd Atk wave increases his attack meaning he can take enemies like Surtr on and deal damage to them, while odd spd wave can help him reach 40 speed (which is a lot for Henry) and should be enough to stop most foes from doubling him, keeping him alive for the next round of combat
His sacred seal should be Hp/Spd 2 as it increases his chances of survival, as it gives him more health and adds a little extra speed increasing the chance that Henry won't get doubled and giving him the chance to strike twice without interruption
builds.a: Life and death 3 / Life and death 4
builds.c: Odd atk wave 3 / odd spd wave 3
